title: How snowflakes form and why no two look alike

sources.title: How do snowflakes form? Get the science behind snow
No two snowflakes are alike. But why?
sources.license: University at Buffalo terms of use (facts only)
sources.note: 事實取自 2026-10-09 搜尋結果中該頁的內容摘錄

facts.text: A snowflake starts when a very cold water droplet freezes onto a tiny particle of dust or pollen in a cloud, forming an ice crystal.
As the ice crystal falls, water vapor freezes onto it and the crystal grows arms.
Snow crystals are six-sided because of the way water molecules arrange themselves when water freezes.
Temperature is the main factor that sets the basic shape of a snow crystal; humidity plays a smaller part.
At some temperatures crystals grow as long, thin needles, while at much colder temperatures they grow as flat plates.
Small changes in temperature or humidity, even over minutes or seconds, can change how the arms of a crystal grow.
All six arms of one snowflake meet the same conditions, so they look alike.
Each snowflake follows a slightly different path to the ground and meets slightly different conditions, so snowflakes tend to look different from one another.
Snowflakes are often photographed under magnification; Wilson Bentley, a farmer, became known for this hobby around 1900.

notes: 訪談中的攝影師是虛構人物（本文由 AI 撰寫），工作方式（用深色布接雪、用軟刷移動、相機加鏡頭、呼氣會使雪花融化、有風時多是碎片）屬一般常識，文中不寫成真人引述。
